I see you've been treated for acute sinusitis with antibiotics, but now you're experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever. Have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as blood, cloudiness, or a strong odor?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of eosinophiluria (binucleated cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm) alongside fever and flank pain strongly suggests acute allergic interstitial nephritis. Given your recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis, did you experience any new skin rash, itching, or joint pain starting a few days after the medication began?

REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine, Liver_Function_Tests
REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the creatinine results; the elevated level confirms significant renal impairment alongside your eosinophiluria and recent antibiotic use. To rule out other causes of flank pain and to assess the extent of kidney damage, did you notice any swelling in your legs or face, and have you experienced any recent high fever with chills?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Allergic Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to antibiotic therapy for sinusitis. The combination of recent antibiotic exposure, fever, flank pain, fatigue, elevated creatinine, and specifically the presence of eosinophiluria (eosinophilic granular cells) confirms this diagnosis.
